Ford Mustang Dragster Races Corvette ZR1 Down the 1/4-Mile, Time To Place Your Bets
7 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels
General Motors has done a fantastic job with the C8-generation Chevrolet Corvette , as not only is the lineup vaster than ever, but it is also more exciting than it has ever been.
The family comprises six distinct versions of the latest model year, and it is the same Stingray that kicks things off. And it packs a new motor, in case you forgot. The small-block V8 has a 6.7-liter displacement this time around, pushing out 535 hp (399 kW/453 ps) and 520 lb-ft (705 Nm) of torque. With the Z51 Performance Pack, which is optional, it needs just 2.8 seconds to reach 60 mph (97 kph). Flat-out, it will do over 200 mph (322+ kph).
That’s basically modern-day supercar territory in something that starts at $71,300 (MSRP). And even its predecessor came with up to 495 hp (369 kW /502 ps), with the 6.2-liter V8 rocketing it to 60 mph in 2.9 seconds. The Grand Sport is next in line, packs the same mill as its lesser sibling, and starts at $86,300. The E-Ray’s successor is the Grand Sport X, and this model comes from $110,000, boasting 721 hp (538 kW/731 ps) in total, and dropping the sprint time to a neck-snapping 2.4 seconds.
Further up, we find the Z06, with its 670 hp (499 kW/679 ps), 2.6 seconds required to hit 60 mph, and an MSRP of $121,800. Sitting at the very top of the lineup is the ZR1X , which features the electric assistance from the discontinued E-Ray, and the Z06’s 5.5-liter V8, albeit with twin turbos. The result is 1,250 hp (933 kW/1,268 ps) and 937 pound-feet (1,270 Nm) of torque in total. 0-60 mph takes 1.89 seconds, the top speed stands at 233 mph (375 kph), and the 1/4-mile is an 8.99-second affair at 157 mph (253 kph).
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels Pricing in this case commences at $227,800, but good luck trying to land one for a bit more over the MSRP, because the dealer markups are insane. The same goes for the lesser Chevy Corvette ZR1. But why haven’t we mentioned it until now? Because it is one of the stars of the video embedded at the bottom of the page.
It kicks off at $198,000, and even if that may be a lot of money, it can actually give supercars that are three times more expensive a real run for their money. From 0 to 60 mph, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 needs just 2.3 seconds. It has 1,064 hp (794 kW/1,079 ps) and 828 lb-ft (1,123 Nm) of torque, and packs a 5.5-liter flat-plane crank V8 with two turbochargers. The top speed is 233 mph (375 kph), and the quarter mile time is 9.6 seconds, with an exit speed of 150 mph (241 kph).
Thus, one must have an insane build if they want to beat the Chevy Corvette ZR1 into submission, but can a Ford Mustang make it to the list? Well, not if we are talking about a bone-stock example, regardless of whether we are talking about the modern-day S650 or the previous-generation, the S550.
This one is part of the latter, and it seems that it started life in the GT configuration , packing a Coyote V8 with 460 horsepower (340 kW/462 ps) available via the right pedal and 420 pound-feet (570 Nm) of torque. The acceleration from 0 to 60 mph took 4.4 seconds, and that makes it a lot slower than its ad-hoc rival, the Corvette ZR1.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels Mind you, one does not have to be a connoisseur to tell that the Ford Mustang GT in question has been visited by the tuning fairy. Not only that, but it is basically a dragster disguised as a muscle car rather than the other way around. It boasts drag radials, has a massive bulge on the hood, and also packs a mandatory parachute to help it stop faster.
We would like to tell you that it has X horsepower and Y torque, but the truth is that we have no idea just how punchy this machine is. And by the looks of it, it is a proper rival to the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 in a head-to-head battle down the quarter mile from a standing start. But is it really anyone’s game?
That is for you to find out by scrolling down to the video shared by Wheels on YouTube and embedded at the bottom of this story. The footage is a little over one and a half minutes long, and if you don’t want to waste your time and jump right into the battle, then you should know that the action starts at the 1:28 mark.
Before clicking the play button, which one of these machines do you think came out victorious? Was it the modern-day ZR1 or the Mustang dragster ? Now, head on down to find out if you were right.
